headings.title: SMTO-EXE-0173 — SMTO can't open this file as a Word, Excel or PowerPoint document

html:
SMTO-EXE-0173 — SMTO can't open this file as a Word, Excel or PowerPoint document

GUID: 9919b530-a920-5370-8a11-7f308b1046f6
Slug: office-invalid-ooxml
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: office

What happened

  • The file isn't a normal, readable .docx, .xlsx or .pptx document. It may be damaged, password-protected or a different file type renamed. SMTO didn't change it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the file in Word, Excel or PowerPoint to check that it opens. If it asks for a password, save a copy with the password removed. SMTO can't open password-protected or damaged files.
  2. Use Save As to save a new copy as .docx, .xlsx or .pptx, especially if the file is an older .doc, .xls or .ppt or was renamed. A fresh save in the modern format repairs the file's internal layout that SMTO checks.
  3. Attach the new copy with Add context, or tell SMTO its exact location, and ask again. SMTO will check the new copy from scratch.

What success looks like

  • SMTO opens the new copy and describes its contents.

If it still fails

  • If even a fresh copy fails, select Copy error details and send them with the file type to the person who manages SMTO. Don't share a password-protected file's password with SMTO; remove the password in your office app instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • OOXML package validation rejected the file (office.invalid_ooxml): malformed or non-ZIP data (including password-protected CFB files), encrypted, unsafe or duplicate ZIP parts, DTDs or entities, inconsistent content types, a missing main part or invalid relationships.

What this means

  • OOXML validation rejected malformed ZIP/XML, unsafe or duplicate parts, encrypted entries, inconsistent content types, missing main parts or invalid relationships. Parsing exceptions also map here. Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.

Why this can happen

  • OOXML validation rejected malformed ZIP/XML, unsafe or duplicate parts, encrypted entries, inconsistent content types, missing main parts or invalid relationships. Parsing exceptions also map here.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect structural package diagnostics and whether extension, main part and content types agree; preserve the original rather than stripping rejected features blindly.

How to fix it

  • Supply a valid DOCX, XLSX or PPTX package whose extension matches its content type, with no encryption, DTD or entities and with valid ZIP parts and relationships. Re-saving from a trusted Office application in the modern format normally produces a valid package.
  • Use a valid DOCX, XLSX or PPTX package with matching extension/content types, no DTD/entities, and valid ZIP parts/relationships.

Retry and execution caution

  • Use a valid DOCX, XLSX or PPTX package with matching extension/content types, no DTD/entities, and valid ZIP parts/relationships.

How to verify the fix

  • A valid supported package passes bounded inspection before structural editing.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay uncertain writes or execute embedded document content.

Technical notes

  • Office workers treat document content as untrusted data and never execute macros or formulas. Publication creates a separate output under existing File policy; retain revision and effect facts before any new write.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
